name: SETA
group: State University of New York (SUNY) at Buffalo, Dept. of Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering (G. Srimathveeravalli, T. Kesavadas, X. Li)
versions: 2010 IJMRCAS (full); the same PI's later SAER robot (UIUC/Buffalo) is robots_A3 saer_sankaran2018; Ashammagari et al. 2016 IMECE automated aortic-arch access on the VIST simulator used a 7-DOF Robai Cyton arm, neither SETA nor SAER (ashammagari2016_image, full)
target_anatomy: neurovascular / endovascular access (design data from femoral-to-internal-carotid angiograms in rabbits and on VIST; srimathveeravalli2010_design Materials and Methods)
devices_driven: guidewire and catheter simultaneously, any standard device 0.014-0.13 in (friction-wheel range); bench: 0.035 in guidewire + 5 Fr Boston Scientific Expo catheter (Results); VIST trial: the manual angiogram (0.035 / 0.014 in Emerald guidewires, 5 Fr Tempo Aqua catheter) repeated with SETA
n_dof_detail: 3 motorised: guidewire insert/withdraw, catheter insert/withdraw, catheter twist (three Maxon EC-22 motors); a travelling cart carrying the guidewire drive and the steering stage runs on a pulley (Design of patient-side slave, Actuators; Fig. 2)
translation_detail: friction-roller: driven lower + idler upper 2 in polyurethane wheels (Shore 55A, mu ~0.6), spring-tensioned self-adjusting housing, normal load 1.275 N (Slave actuators; Fig. 3)
rotation_detail: catheter only: miniature gripper of brass roller pins on O-ring-tensioned steel shafts (transmits torque, allows axial slip) turned by a pulley from a servomotor and torque sensor (Slave actuators; Fig. 4)
force_sensing: proximal: LXT 971 torque sensor (Cooper Instruments, +/-2.5 Nm, 0.005 Nm resolution) between each motor and its wheel/pulley, converted to axial and radial tool forces (Slave actuators; Teleoperation)
haptics_leader: Novint Falcon; twist mapped to left-right stylus motion; force-reflecting loop at 500 Hz with Butterworth tremor filter (5-25 Hz), motion scaling and delay term (Teleoperation and haptic feedback, Eq. 1, Fig. 5)
validation_detail: bench: step inputs to 30/60/90 mm at 1000/2500/5000 rpm, 15 repeats each, plus ramps (Fig. 6); steering 1 deg steps over 360 deg, 10 cycles each way on a 5 F catheter (Fig. 7); phantom: teleoperated 0.035 in guidewire in a silicone vessel with one bifurcation (Fig. 8); VIST simulator: 8 neurovascular surgeons and fellows (7 M, 1 F, mean 500 cases) repeated a carotid angiogram, procedure time 87.42 s robotic vs 80.57 s manual (p = 0.829), contrast 7 vs 5.75 cc (p = 0.723), 1 participant did not finish; questionnaire 2.25-3.0 of 4 (Table 3, Fig. 11). In vivo animal studies only planned (Abstract, Conclusion)
key_numbers: insertion slip < 0.4 mm per 100 mm; teleoperated phantom lag < 0.003 in; back-slip force 0.76 N (4x below the 3 N tool limit, so buckling stays outside the lumen); EC-22 motors 18,000 rpm max with 1:128 gearhead (~3 Nm); friction-wheel assembly 130 g; teleoperation 500 Hz; master spec from motion study: 28.5 mm stroke, 4.5 N, 13 Hz hand motion (Slave actuators, Teleoperation, Results)
sim_model: none found (VIST simulator used as the test patient, not a model of SETA)
